featured_reviews.name: Keya Phatnani
featured_reviews.review_text:
We have been using Healkin for the past 6 months for both home nursing support and caregiver services, and our experience has been consistently excellent. The staff has been professional, compassionate, dependable, and extremely patient in handling day-to-day care needs.

What truly stands out is the responsiveness and sense of responsibility of their coordination team. On one occasion, due to an unforeseen last-minute issue with the scheduled nurse for the next day, Krithika went the extra mile late at night and arranged a replacement to ensure there was absolutely no disruption in care. That level of commitment and ownership gave us tremendous peace of mind.

Over the months, we have found the nurses to be clinically competent and attentive, while the caregivers have been warm, respectful, and genuinely caring towards the patient and family alike. Managing home care over an extended period can be stressful, and having a reliable agency like this has made a meaningful difference for us.

Would highly recommend Healkin to anyone looking for trustworthy home healthcare and caregiving support.

Due to its progressive nature & lack of medical treatments, caring for those with Dementia is critical. In Mumbai, Dignity Foundation is successfully running a Dementia Day Care Centre, catering to the unmet needs of the city.
Our Dementia Day Care Centre is staffed with trained caregivers who provide elder care with compassion. They manage members’ mood swings, aggression & other behavioural symptoms successfully.
We offer home pick-up and drop service along with daily lunch and refreshments. Members get therapies & engage in social interactions to stay active. We have other centres in New Delhi, Pune, Kolkata and Chennai.

featured_reviews.name: B D
featured_reviews.review_text:
Our experience with Alpha was shocking - a nightmare - very disappointing.

We heard of Alpha Care Home in 2022. At that time it looked like the best place for our family member. But within 1 year we faced serious problems.

Biggest issue is that Alpha does not have 24-hour caretakers. For a place with so many elderly & medically unfit people, this is unacceptable. All carehomes must have 24 hour help and monitoring.

There is also no proper introduction between the residents. There is no separation of people based on their needs. People with mental health problems and those bed ridden are kept together with normal people. This is extremely unsafe.

One night, our family member was locked out of his room until 2 a.m. His roommate, who had mental issues, did not allow him to enter. We told Amis Lopes, but no action was taken. Our complaint was conveniently ignored.

Later, a much worse incident happened. Our family member was beaten. He was hit, pushed against a wall, and his face was swollen. His glasses and hearing aids were damaged. At that time, nobody was present to help. Amis Lopes was out of town, and there was no helper or caretaker.

Unacceptable & a serious matter. Amis Lopes was liable for a police case & interrogation, due to his negligence and inadequate staff our family was injured. Such incidents are a crime in a care home.

Alpha is an unclean and overcrowded care home with no 24-hour care staff. The owner is kind in the beginning during admission and payments, but later was completely disappointing and untrustworthy.

featured_reviews.name: Avrel Almeida
featured_reviews.review_text:
Horrible experience with the main Dr (owner) cheating the patient.  It has a long list of problems faced there, but few main points that I would want to highlight. Just to give a little background to understand, the patient was asked to admit at this nursing at home due to the medical history of diabetes and the patient was asked to take complete rest, medicine and food was to be given from time to time, since the patient was not being obedient at home, the patient was asked to get admitted. 1st main issue - During the stay of 3 days at the nursing home, the owner Dr. didn't even think it imp to go through the medical file & check the case history of the patient. One medicine given to the patient was incorrect and one which had to be given was not given during the admission in that nursing home for 3 full days. Upon questioning regarding the wrong medicine given he said "pan patient la kai zala tar nahi na??"... Means nothing happened to the patient na???. Plz tell me who says this..   2nd- He didn't even touch the patient as the treating Dr was different and the owner Dr did not treat the patient as it was not required infact he spoke to the patient only on the first day of admission. And for that he charged a lump sum consultation amount in the bill. 3rd- He did not informed the treating Dr that his patient was admitted, but kept telling us that he would speak to the treating Dr, then he said her number was not reachable, then not connecting and this went on for 3 days, finally I directly called up the patient's dr and spoke to her. 4th - in the room, there were lots of mosquitoes, but he was very hesitant to put a repellent machine. After several reminders and request the machine was finally given. The fan in that room was very
very slow, the fan regulator had an issue but he didn't want to change or repair it (all rooms are non AC) there were many rooms that were empty, hence we kept requesting him if we could change to the side room whose fan was working fine, but till the end that man did not accept our request and made us sleep in the same room with the slow fan in such hot climate conditions. This owner dr is a very stingy, rude, forgetful (he won't forget to empty your pocket while billing- he literally charges extra if the patient's clothes are washed there, if the guest has bathed in the nursing home's bathroom, also it seems that there are different prices of the same room for different patient this we got to know through another patient) and a very arrogance person if you question him or remind him of anything. You'll find him as a sweet person as long as you give in to all his demands and during the admission.. the food was also not enough in quantity compared to the price change. But overall if we have to be careful and cross check medications given like a nurse then y would we trust the Dr and get the patient admitted. One last point, the siringe used for diabetics blood test is the same one for all 3 days. Since the nursing home don't have much patients they can manage keeping 1 siringe for per patient till the discharge. After asking the Dr abt this he said "the nurse opens the pack at the reception and then brings it to the room for checking", which never seemed the case to me. So yes if possible please AVOID THIS PLACE.
